results.name: device_group_add_device
results.evidence: in_CX indexes scenario->device_groups block (count at DAT_00746f8c+0x36c, pointer +0x370, stride 0x40); allocates/reuses a 100-byte membership datum via datum_new, copies group def fields (+0x20 type,+0x24,+0x38) into it and picks a vtable handler at PTR_PTR_00686fe8[type-1], then sets grid/object flag bits (+0x204 bit 0x40/0x8000000) tying object in_EAX to the group
results.summary: Attaches an object (register eax = object id, ecx = scenario device_group index) to a device group, allocating a new membership record if none exists and initializing it from the scenario device_groups definition.

results.name: device_groups_update
results.evidence: Walks the same membership list via data_iterator_next, validates each entry's object id against the live object table and calls datum_delete on stale/invalid entries, otherwise advances the group's interpolation state through the PTR_PTR_00686fe8 vtable and calls object_get_position/FUN_00569bf0 for dependent object updates
results.summary: Per-tick maintenance pass over all device group membership records: removes entries for dead objects and advances the live ones' group value/position state.

results.name: device_group_has_active_member
results.evidence: Iterates data_iterator_next looking for a membership record whose object id (+4) equals the register-passed target and whose flag byte (+0xa) bit0 is clear, returning a bool; used by FUN_0044a930 before creating a new record
results.summary: Searches the device-group membership list for an active (non-pending-delete) record matching a given object id and returns whether one exists.

results.name: device_group_find_member
results.evidence: Same iteration pattern as FUN_0044acc0 but matches on object id alone (no flag check) and returns the found node pointer in EAX (Ghidra shows void return but caller assigns the result), writing -1 into an optional out parameter when not found
results.summary: Looks up a device-group membership record by object id, returning the record pointer (via EAX) and optionally writing -1 to *param_1 if none is found.

results.name: device_null_function
results.evidence: Function body is a single ret with no parameters, locals, or globals referenced; 3 callers elsewhere in the binary suggest it is used as a default/no-op entry in a function-pointer table (compare the PTR_PTR_00686fe8 vtable used by neighboring device-group functions)
results.summary: Empty function that immediately returns; likely a no-op placeholder used as a default callback.

results.name: device_maybe_change_power_state
results.evidence: Loads the object's device tag definition (tag id from object+0 through the DAT_0087bc14 tag-instance table, +0x14 gets the definition pointer) and only calls FUN_0044ae30 (the power state change routine) when definition field +0x292 is zero
results.summary: Guard function that invokes the device power-state change routine only when a flag/field at offset 0x292 of the device's tag definition is zero.

results.name: device_change_power_state
results.evidence: Reads device definition field +0x290 (a 0..3 type enum) to pick between the group's current power value (DAT_0087abf0 table) compared to 0.5, or a fixed 0.0/1.0, or a custom value at +0x294, then calls FUN_0044bd70 to write it into the device's group value table and FUN_0044c1a0 to trigger the associated state-change effect/sound
results.summary: Computes a target power value for the device (auto-threshold, forced on/off, or a custom definition value) and applies it via the group value setter, then plays the state-change effect/sound.

results.name: device_machine_update
results.evidence: Blends puVar5[0x7f] (power fraction) into puVar5[0x82] (position value, matches the position_group cache field set up by device_new at object+0x208), scans object_find_in_sphere for nearby objects to auto-open (calls FUN_0044bd70(1.0f) then sets puVar5[0x86]=-3), and finally propagates the device's own position delta to any riders whose parent field (+0x4d4) equals this object, translating their cached positions via FUN_004f5de0/FUN_004f5c30
results.summary: Per-object tick update for a device machine: advances its automatic-open proximity check, tracks how long it has sat fully open before auto-closing, and moves any objects riding on it by the device's frame-to-frame position delta.

results.name: device_apply_initial_open_flag
results.evidence: Checks object flag byte (+0x214) bit3 and a valid position group index (+0x204 != -1) before calling FUN_0044bea0(1.0f), the immediate group-value setter, matching a 'starts open' placement flag being applied once at spawn
results.summary: If the device's placement flags mark it as starting open and it has a valid position group, forces that group's value to 1.0 immediately.

results.name: device_update_change_values
results.evidence: Operates on the same power (word offsets 0x7e/0x7f = byte 0x1f8/0x1fc) and position (0x81..0x84 = byte 0x204..0x210) fields set up by device_new, calling FUN_004cf360 (a rate-limited approach/lerp helper) against definition rate parameters (+0x274..0x288) and firing FUN_0044c1a0 on reaching thresholds or after a delay counter overflow
results.summary: Advances the device's cached power and position values toward their target group values at a rate governed by the tag definition, returning whether the position is still settling and triggering state-change effects along the way.

results.name: device_get_change_function_values
results.evidence: Reads up to 4 function-type codes from the device definition at +0x198 and, per case (1=power value 0x7f, 2=abs power delta/rate via +0x278, 3=position value 0x82, 4=abs position delta/rate via +0x288, 5=door-open combination of group/flag state, 6=stuck-counter ratio via +0x28c), writes a computed float into the output array at puVar3+0x49 (object+0x124)
results.summary: Evaluates the device's configured animation-driver functions (power, position, their rates, and a door-state function) into an output float array used to drive model/shader animation.

results.name: device_group_set_value
results.evidence: Clamps param_1 to [0,1], compares against the current value at DAT_0087abf0[unaff_SI], and if different sets the 'changing' flag bit1 in the group's flag word and iterates every object via object_iterator_next to call FUN_0044c1a0 for any whose position group (+0x1f8 offset in that iteration struct) equals the modified group
results.summary: Sets a device group's shared value (power or position, selected by the caller-supplied group index), marking it as changing and broadcasting the state-change effect/sound to all objects that reference that group.

results.name: device_group_set_value_immediate
results.evidence: Clamps param_1 to [0,1] and writes it straight into DAT_0087abf0[unaff_SI].value without the equality check FUN_0044bd70 does, then walks all objects and force-sets their per-object cached power (+0x1fc) or position (+0x208) value and resets the associated delta/counter whenever their group index (+0x1f8 or +0x204) matches
results.summary: Hard-sets a device group's value and immediately resyncs every object referencing that group as either its power or position group, bypassing the normal interpolated transition.

results.name: device_new
results.evidence: Reads a placement/definition struct (unaff_EDI): field0 = power_group_index (-1 -> datum_new a fresh group), field1 = position_group_index (same pattern), stores them at object+0x1f8/+0x204, mirrors their current group values into the cached fields object+0x1fc/+0x208, and sets object flag bits (+500) from placement flag bits 3 and 4
results.summary: Initializes a newly created device object's power and position group links (allocating new groups if unassigned) and copies the initial group values and flags onto the object.

results.name: device_control_maybe_update
results.evidence: Reads object field +0xb4 (a short object-subtype code) and only calls FUN_0044adf0 when it equals 8, matching Blam's object type enum where machine=7 and control=8, explicitly excluding machines with the 'sVar1 != 7' check
results.summary: Dispatches to the device power-change guard only for device_control objects (object subtype 8), skipping device_machine objects (subtype 7).

results.name: device_can_change_position
results.evidence: Looks up the object's position group flags (+0x204 -> DAT_0087abf0 table +2) requiring bits 0 and 1 both set to allow change, clears the result if the object's own flag bit1 (+500) is set, and also clears it unless the object's power group value equals 1.0 (0x3f800000)
results.summary: Determines whether a device is allowed to change its position, requiring its position group to be in the right lock/change state, an unset local block flag, and full power (power group value == 1.0).

results.name: device_frontfacing
results.evidence: cea-pdb hint 'device_frontfacing' via string 'front'; code fetches a unit via object_try_and_get(0x100), skips if the unit's flag byte (+0x214) bit0 is set, gets its forward vector via FUN_004f6080, and returns 0 only when the dot product of that vector with unaff_EDI (the device's own facing normal) is positive
results.summary: Checks whether a nearby unit is facing the front side of a one-sided device, returning 0 (allowed) when the unit's forward vector points toward the device's front.

results.name: device_play_state_change_effect
results.evidence: Looks up the tag group fourCC of tag id in_ECX via the DAT_0087bc14 tag-instance table (*(int*)(id*0x20+base)) and compares it against 0x65666665 ('effe', the effect tag group) to call FUN_004507a0, or 0x736e6421 ('snd!', the sound tag group) to call FUN_00543ce0
results.summary: Given a tag id (register ecx), dispatches to the effect-creation routine if it names an effect tag, or the sound-playback routine if it names a sound tag; used to play a device's state-change effect or sound.

results.name: device_groups_initialize
results.evidence: Loops over a scenario tag block (count at DAT_00746f8c+0x288, pointer +0x28c, stride 0x34) calling datum_new for each entry to populate the shared device-group value table (DAT_0087abf0), seeding each new slot's flags from the block entry's byte at +0x24
results.summary: Allocates and initializes the runtime device-group value table from the scenario's device group definitions at level load.
